mainEntity.name: How much does a Vauxhall Astra 1.2 Turbo engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Vauxhall Astra 1.2 Turbo engine replacement typically costs £1,500-£2,800 supply-only for a rebuilt unit (EB2ADTS / F12SHT), with used engines from £400-£900. Fitting adds approximately £390-£650 in labour (6-10 hours at independent specialist rates). Main dealer fitted prices are typically 30-50% higher.

mainEntity.name: How much does a Vauxhall Astra 1.4 Turbo engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Vauxhall Astra 1.4 Turbo engine replacement costs £1,500-£3,000 supply-only for a rebuilt unit (A14NET / B14XFT / B14XFL). Used engines start from £300-£800. Fitting adds approximately £455-£715 in labour (7-11 hours). Some owners report dealer quotes of £6,000-£7,000 for a new engine, making specialist-supplied rebuilt units significantly more cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: How much does a Vauxhall Astra 1.5 Turbo D engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Vauxhall Astra 1.5 Turbo D engine replacement costs £2,500-£4,000 supply-only for a rebuilt unit (DV5RC / F15DVH), with used engines from £500-£1,200. Fitting adds approximately £520-£780 in labour (8-12 hours). DPF and AdBlue system repairs are a more common (and cheaper) fix than full engine replacement on this engine.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of wet belt failure in a Vauxhall Astra 1.2 Turbo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include a rattling noise from the timing cover on cold start, oil pressure warning light flashing, poor engine performance, and in severe cases, complete engine seizure. The 1.2 PureTech wet belt should be inspected at every service and replaced preventatively at 60,000 miles or 6 years.

mainEntity.name: What is LSPI and why does it affect the Astra 1.4 Turbo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low-speed pre-ignition (LSPI) is a phenomenon where the air-fuel mixture in the combustion chamber ignites prematurely under high load at low engine speeds. On the Astra 1.4 Turbo (especially B14XFT), LSPI can cause cracked pistons and catastrophic engine failure. Using the correct API SN Plus or SP grade oil and avoiding lugging the engine at low RPM can reduce risk.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Vauxhall Astra 1.2-1.5 Turbo?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 2015-2022 Astra worth £5,000-£15,000, a rebuilt engine at £1,500-£4,000 plus fitting may represent 30-60% of the vehicle's value. For Mk VIII Astra L (2022+) worth £12,000-£22,000, replacement is almost always viable. For older Mk VI Astra J (pre-2016) with values under £4,000, a used engine may be more cost-effective than a rebuilt unit.

historyTimeline.h2: Vauxhall Astra 1.2-1.5 Turbo - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Vauxhall Astra 1.2-1.5 Turbo range spans two generations of the popular family hatchback - the Mk VII (Astra K, 2015-2022) and the Mk VIII (Astra L, 2022-present). The turbocharged petrol and diesel engines in this range replaced older naturally aspirated and CDTi units, offering improved efficiency, lower emissions and stronger low-end torque.

milestones.description: Mk VII Astra K launched with 1.4 Turbo petrol (A14NET, 140PS) and 1.6 CDTi diesel; 1.2 Turbo (F12SHT, 131PS) and 1.4 Turbo (B14XFT, 150PS) join the range
Mk VII facelift introduces 1.5 Turbo D diesel (DV5RC / F15DVH, 130PS) replacing the 1.6 CDTi; 1.2 Turbo updated to EB2ADTS (130PS) with revised emissions hardware
Mk VIII Astra L launched with 1.2 Turbo petrol (EB2ADTS, 110PS & 130PS) and 1.5 Turbo D diesel (DV5RC, 130PS) as the core engine line-up
1.4 Turbo petrol phased out in favour of 1.2 Turbo across most trims

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Vauxhall Astra 1.2-1.5 Turbo range is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Vauxhall Astra 1.2-1.5 Turbo Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Vauxhall Astra 1.2-1.5 Turbo range covers both petrol (1.2/1.4) and diesel (1.5) engines across the Mk VII (K) and Mk VIII (L) generations. Petrol owners report wet belt degradation (1.2) and LSPI / timing chain issues (1.4), while diesel owners face DPF clogging and AdBlue system failures. Rebuilt Astra 1.2-1.5 Turbo engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: 1.2 Turbo Wet Belt Degradation - Why the Vauxhall Astra 1.2 Turbo Fails Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The 1.2 PureTech engine uses a timing belt that runs in engine oil (a "wet belt"). Over time, the belt degrades and sheds debris into the oil system, clogging the oil pickup strainer. This starves the engine of oil, leading to turbo failure, timing jump or complete engine seizure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing belt, tensioner and oil pump belt; clean oil pickup
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended every 6 years or 60,000 miles - cheapest option
When belt has failed and caused oil starvation damage

problems.recommendation: For 1.2 Turbo owners, preventative wet belt replacement at 60,000 miles or 6 years is the most cost-effective approach - it costs a fraction of a full engine replacement. For 1.4 Turbo owners with LSPI or timing chain symptoms, early diagnosis is critical; catching chain stretch before it jumps can save thousands. For 1.5 diesel owners, regular motorway driving to allow DPF regeneration and using the correct AdBlue specification will extend component life. If the car is a Mk VI Astra J (pre-2016) worth under £4,000, a used engine may be more economically sensible than a rebuilt unit.

problems.h4: 1.4 Turbo LSPI & Timing Chain Issues - Vauxhall Astra 1.4 Turbo Engine Failure
problems.rootCause: Low-speed pre-ignition (LSPI) can cause cracked pistons, particularly on the B14XFT engine. Timing chain stretch and tensioner failure are common on A14NET and B14XFT units, often triggered by low oil pressure or incorrect oil grade.

problems.h4: 1.5 Turbo D DPF & AdBlue System Issues - Vauxhall Astra 1.5 Diesel Problems
